questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"In the Ain-i-Akbari, Abul Fazl describes the corporate functioning of the Mughal village community: 'The village headman, known as the muqaddam or mandal, was chosen through the consensus of the village elders, and this choice had to be ratified by the zamindar. The headman held his office as long as he enjoyed the confidence of the village elders, failing which he could be dismissed. His chief function was to supervise the preparation of village accounts, assisted by the patwari (accountant). The village had a common financial pool (kisaan-i kamil or common fund) to which each individual cultivator contributed. Out of this pool were met the expenses for entertaining revenue officials who visited the village from time to time, as well as community welfare expenses like building bunds or digging irrigation canals.'"

options.text: Funding private trade expeditions to Central Asia
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Purchasing European firearms for village youth
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Village Administration and Common Fund (The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society (Peasants, Zamindars and State)):
1. The fund covered community hospitality expenses for inspecting officials and financed shared infrastructure like dikes and irrigation canals.
Hence Option B is correct.

The British government was asked to protect the honour of innocent women and children.
